Five-star service and delicious dim sum at a reasonable price
May 2026 • Couples
We had another amazing dim sum lunch at Chit Chat. The main waitress named Sandy and her team provided excellent five-star service. Our drinks were always quickly refilled and empty dishes were taken away promptly. We stayed a bit longer than we should have, but they did not make us feel rushed at all. We really appreciated their diligent and cheerful service, it is one of the things that makes Chit Chat such a relaxing place to dine. The restaurant is also very elegant and spotlessly clean.

The dim sum buffet is an excellent deal. I think there were over 50 dishes to choose from, and they are made to order. All of the dumplings and rolls were delicious, especially the ones with abalone, scallops and shrimp. They even provided gloves for one of the prawn dishes so you could peel them without getting your hands dirty. The food wasn't too salty, which is often the case with other Chinese restaurants (which is great if you're watching your blood pressure!). The desserts were also unique and tasty, not overly sweet, especially the mango pudding, the egg tarts and the "carrot cake" (a glutinous rice cake in the shape of a carrot with black bean filling, really yummy). All four of us thoroughly enjoyed our meal. The buffet also includes iced tea (the lychee iced tea is really refreshing) or hot tea. I love that they don't nickel-and-dime you with high drink prices like other high-end dim sum places. We live in the city and have been here several times, and have never been disappointed. We look forward to coming back soon!

Visited twice, will return
Dec 2016 • Couples
We first ate here at Easter last year, where we enjoyed the amazing buffet and our daughter was thrilled with the special activities for children. Of particular note that day were the 3 varieties of in-house smoked salmons. 

We returned last night for a quiet dinner buffet. The food was simply fantastic. From fresh sashimi, to incredibly tender and moist duck, to the cooked-to-order grill serving lamb, jumbo prawns, steak, scallops, and more. It was certainly a feast we enjoyed. One highlight is the pretzel bread--it's probably the best bread we've had in Saigon, and we were able to buy some to take home with us afterwards. 

One suggestion would be to look at the method for making lattes. The coffee was not very strong or hot, and I think that it should be improved for the type of the hotel that this is. The best coffee we've had at a 5 star hotel in Saigon is the Caravelle. It wouldn't be remiss to send someone over to their lounge and taste the difference in order to improve the coffee at the Equatorial. The desserts are also a bit uninspired and quite typical for Asia where they look better than they taste. It would be nice if there were more European recipes for the sweets. 

Service was prompt and courteous. Music was perfect for the setting. We will definitely return. We have eaten most of the dinner buffets at the 4 and 5 star hotels in Saigon, and this is a favorite. While the buffet might not be massive, the quality and variety didn't disappoint.

The Chit Chat Cafe is inside HCMC's Equatorial Hotel and offers a complimentary breakfast buffet for guests (plus other meals as well). There are an array of both western style offerings plus Asian (Vietnamese & Chinese) dishes, fruit, pastries, etc. A number of hot food selections varied each day, and there was a good number of tasty accompaniments for your morning rice porridge.
